title: PPF: Building a Child's Corpus with ₹1.5 Lakh Annual Contributions
description: The Public Provident Fund (PPF) is a popular, tax-efficient savings scheme for long-term goals in India. Contributing the maximum ₹1.5 lakh annually to a PPF .

faq.q: Can I open more than one PPF account for my minor children?
faq.a: No, a parent or guardian can open only one PPF account for a minor child. The parent themselves can also only hold one PPF account.

faq.q: What is the maximum I can contribute to a minor's PPF account?
faq.a: The maximum combined contribution to your own PPF account and any minor's PPF account(s) linked to your name is ₹1.5 lakh in a financial year.

faq.q: Is the interest rate on PPF fixed for the entire 15 years?
faq.a: No, the interest rate on PPF is not fixed for 15 years. It is reviewed and declared quarterly by the Ministry of Finance and can change.

faq.q: Can I withdraw money from a minor's PPF account before maturity?
faq.a: Partial withdrawals are allowed from the 7th financial year onwards, subject to certain conditions and limits. Full withdrawal is only at maturity after 15 years.

faq.q: What happens to the minor's PPF account when they turn 18?
faq.a: When the minor turns 18, the account status changes from 'minor' to 'major'. The erstwhile minor (now major) will need to submit an application along with KYC documents to the bank or post office to regularise the account.

faq.q: Are NRIs allowed to open a PPF account?
faq.a: No, Non-Resident Indians (NRIs) are generally not allowed to open new PPF accounts. However, if a resident Indian becomes an NRI after opening a PPF account, they can continue the account until its maturity.

faq.q: Is the PPF interest compounded monthly or annually?
faq.a: PPF interest is compounded annually, but it is calculated monthly on the lowest balance between the 5th and the last day of the month.
